modern-en.context: DUKE. To explain to you the principles of government would seem like me making a show of fine speeches, since I know that your own expertise in this exceeds anything my advice could add. So nothing remains but to trust your sufficiency to act as your worth allows, and let your judgment do its work. The character of our people, our city's institutions, and the standards of common justice — in all these you are as well versed as study and experience have ever made anyone we know. Here is your commission, from which we don't want you to stray. Call him here, I say — bid Angelo come before us. [Exit an Attendant.] What kind of stand-in for me do you think he will make? For you should know, we have with special care chosen him to take our place in our absence; we've lent him our authority, dressed him in our love, and given his deputation every instrument of our own power. What do you think of it?
